source.title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds

accepted.question_text: Let C4 = <sigma> act freely on S^2 x S^2 by sigma(x,y) = (y,-x), and let M be the quotient manifold. Let RP^2 embed in M by [x] -> [x,x], let N be its tangent disk-bundle neighborhood, and write M as N union MCyl(L(4,1) -> L(8,1)), where MCyl denotes the mapping cylinder of the indicated double cover of lens spaces. Let M0 = N union MCyl(L(4,1) -> L(8,3)), a smooth manifold homotopy equivalent to M. Are M and M0 homeomorphic? Are they diffeomorphic?

evidence.quote: Let C4 = <sigma> act freely on S2 x S2 with that action of sigma defined by the equation sigma(x,y) = (y,-x) and let M be the quotient manifold.
The smooth manifold M0 = N union MCyl(L(4,1) -> L(8,3)) is homotopy equivalent to M. Question. Are M and M0 homeomorphic? diffeomorphic?

accepted.question_text: For Cat equal to Top, PL, or Diff, call a Cat-manifold irreducible when every connected-sum decomposition of it has at least one summand that is a homotopy sphere. In dimension 3, the Kneser-Milnor theorem says that every compact Cat 3-manifold decomposes as a connected sum of irreducible 3-manifolds and that the decomposition is unique up to permutation of summands. To what extent do the existence and uniqueness parts of this connected-sum decomposition theorem hold for compact Cat-manifolds in dimensions at least 4, allowing the formulation to be taken up to homotopy spheres?

evidence.quote: Let Cat be one of the categories Top, PL or Diff. A Cat-manifold M is called irreducible if, whenever we can write M as a connected sum of Cat-manifolds at least one of the summands is a homotopy sphere.

The Kneser-Milnor theorem says that every compact Cat 3-manifold admits a connected sum decomposition into irreducible 3-manifolds, and this connected sum decomposition is unique up to permutation of the summands. Stefan Friedl asked to what degree this statement holds in higher dimensions.

accepted.question_text: For trisections of 4-manifolds, determine analogues of Casson-Gordon theory for Heegaard splittings: identify properties of trisections that have strong topological consequences, such as simplifying the trisection or producing useful topological information, and that can be recognized from local information such as a trisection diagram.

evidence.quote: A key concept introduced in the theory by Casson and Gordon was the notion of strong irreducibility

The challenge for the analogous theory of trisections of 4-manifold is to determine properties of trisections that have strong topological consequences and that can be determined by local information, for instance, from a trisection diagram.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed aspherical manifold whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre. Does M have a finite cover that admits a principal S^1-action?
accepted.context_brief: Aspherical manifolds with central fundamental group

evidence.quote: Given a closed aspherical manifold M whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre, we can ask the following: Question A. Does there exist a finite cover of M with a principal S1-action?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed aspherical manifold whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre. Is M null-cobordant, that is, does its cobordism class vanish?

evidence.quote: Given a closed aspherical manifold M whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre, we can ask the following: Question B. Is such an M null-cobordant?

accepted.question_text: For a closed smooth 4-manifold M, define the trisection genus of M to be the minimal genus of the central surface appearing in a trisection of M. Is trisection genus additive under connected sum of closed smooth 4-manifolds?

evidence.quote: Let M be a closed smooth 4-manifold. The "trisection genus" of M is the minimal genus of the central surface appearing in a trisection of M. Question. Is the trisection genus additive under connected sum?

accepted.question_text: Consider compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary in the setting where the Borel conjecture for pairs is valid by topological surgery, namely when the common fundamental group pi = pi1(M0) is good, for example elementary amenable. Which good groups pi occur as fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds?

evidence.quote: By topological surgery, the Borel Conjecture is valid when the fundamental group pi = pi1(M0) is good, for example, if pi is elementary amenable. One now proceeds to the following three problems: 1. Decide which good pi are the fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds.

accepted.question_text: For compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary, in the same setting where topological surgery applies to good fundamental groups, what groups can occur as the fundamental groups of the boundary components?

evidence.quote: One now proceeds to the following three problems: 1. Decide which good pi are the fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds. 2. Determine the possible fundamental groups of the boundary components.

accepted.question_text: For compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary, in the same setting where topological surgery applies to good fundamental groups, what homeomorphism types can occur among the boundary components?

evidence.quote: 2. Determine the possible fundamental groups of the boundary components. 3. Determine the homeomorphism types of the boundary components.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to M necessarily diffeomorphic to M?

evidence.quote: Question. Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to M diffeomorphic to M? The question has not been answered for any M, not even the 4-torus.

accepted.question_text: Let Sigma be an integral homology 3-sphere that is not homeomorphic to S^3. Does there exist a locally flat embedding Sigma -> S^4 such that one or both complementary regions are not simply connected?

evidence.quote: Question. Let Sigma be an integral homology 3-sphere, not homeomorphic to S3. Is there a locally flat embedding Sigma -> S4 such that one or both complementary regions are not simply-connected?

accepted.question_text: Let L be a stably slice link in S^3, meaning that for some n >= 0 the components of L bound disjoint locally flat nullhomologous disks in D^4 # n(S^2 x S^2), where a disk in a compact 4-manifold W with boundary S^3 is nullhomologous when its relative fundamental class in H2(W, boundary W; Z) vanishes. Let sn(L) be the minimal such n. For stably slice links with more than one component, does sn(L) <= g_top_4(L), the topological four-genus of L, always hold?

evidence.quote: A link L in S3 is stably slice if there exists n >= 0 such that the components of L bound a collection of disjoint locally flat nullhomologous discs in the manifold D4#n(S2 x S2). The stabilising number sn(L) of a stably slice link is the minimal such n.
Question A. Does the inequality sn(L) <= gtop4(L) hold for stably slice links L of more than one component?

accepted.question_text: For knots, the stabilising number can be defined in both the topological category and the smooth category, with the smooth version requiring the bounding disks to be smoothly embedded. Is there a knot K with Arf invariant zero that is not topologically slice and satisfies 0 < sn_top(K) < sn_smooth(K), so that the topological and smooth stabilising numbers differ?

evidence.quote: Remark. The definition of the stabilising number also makes sense in the smooth category (one requires that the discs be smoothly embedded).

Question B. Is there a difference between the topological and smooth stabilising numbers of a knot? More precisely, is there a non-topological slice, Arf invariant zero knot K such that 0 < sntop(K) < snsmooth(K)?

accepted.question_text: Give a satisfactory proof that any two locally flat topological embeddings of a closed oriented surface in S^4 whose complement has infinite cyclic fundamental group are homeomorphic.

evidence.quote: Kawauchi has published several accounts of the theorem below; however, none of them are satisfactory. The problem is to give a satisfactory proof.
Theorem. Any two locally flat topological embeddings of a closed oriented surface in S4 whose complement has infinite cyclic fundamental group are homeomorphic.

accepted.question_text: Complex conjugation on CP^2 has fixed set RP^2 and orbit space S^4, and the analogous involution on aCP^2 # bCP^2 gives a locally flat embedding of the connected sum of a+b copies of RP^2 in S^4. Is every locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S^4 whose complement has fundamental group of order 2 homeomorphic to one of these embeddings?

evidence.quote: The involution on aCP2#bCP2 thus gives a locally flat embedding of #a+bRP2 in S4.
Conjecture. Any locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S4 whose complement has order 2 fundamental group is homeomorphic to one of the above embeddings.

accepted.question_text: For q >= 2, work with connected compact smooth 2q-manifolds. For a natural number g, let W_g be the connected sum of g copies of S^q x S^q. Two compact smooth 2q-manifolds M0 and M1 with the same Euler characteristic are stably diffeomorphic if M0 # W_g is diffeomorphic to M1 # W_g for some g >= 0. The stable class S_st(M) consists of diffeomorphism classes of 2q-manifolds with the same Euler characteristic as M that are stably diffeomorphic to M, and cancellation holds for M when this stable class has exactly one element. The genus g(M) is the largest g such that M is diffeomorphic to M0 # W_g for some compact smooth 2q-manifold M0. For a finitely presented group pi and epsilon in {+1,-1}, define the epsilon-cancellation genus cg_epsilon(pi) to be the minimum genus bound g0 such that cancellation holds for every 2q-manifold M with epsilon = (-1)^q, pi1(M) is isomorphic to pi, and g(M) >= g0, if such a bound exists, and infinity otherwise. Is there a finitely presented group pi that is not polycyclic-by-finite and nevertheless has cg_epsilon(pi) < infinity for some epsilon?

evidence.quote: For a natural number g, define Wg := #g(Sq x Sq) to be the g-fold connected sum of Sq x Sq with itself.
Problem A. (Genus bounds for general groups) Is there an example of a finitely presented group pi which is not polycyclic-by-finite and for which cg_epsilon(pi) < infinity for some epsilon?

accepted.question_text: Using the same cancellation-genus setup for connected compact smooth 2q-manifolds, is there a finitely presented group pi and epsilon in {+1,-1} for which the epsilon-cancellation genus cg_epsilon(pi) is at least 2? Equivalently, can one find 2q-manifolds M and N with fundamental group pi such that M # W_g is diffeomorphic to N # W_g for some g, but M # W_1 and N # W_1 are not diffeomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem B. (Is the cancellation genus ever greater than one?) Is there a finitely presented group pi and epsilon in {+/-1} such that cg_epsilon(pi) >= 2?
i.e. is there a pair of 2q-manifolds M and N with pi1(M) isomorphic to pi1(N) isomorphic to pi such that we have M#Wg isomorphic to N#Wg for some g but M#W1 and N#W1 are not diffeomorphic?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed connected compact 2q-manifold, let pi = pi1(M), let w1 be its orientation character, and let S_st(M) be the stable class of M: diffeomorphism classes of 2q-manifolds with the same Euler characteristic as M that become diffeomorphic to M after connected sum with some W_g = #g(S^q x S^q). The surgery L-group L_{2q+1}(Z[pi], w1) acts on S_st(M) by Wall realisation. Determine the orbit set S_st(M) / L_{2q+1}(Z[pi], w1).
accepted.context_brief: L-group orbits on the stable class

evidence.quote: Recall that pi = pi1(M) and w1 = w1(M) are the fundamental group and orientation character of M and that the L-group L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) acts on the stable class of M via Wall realisation
Problem. Determine Sst(M)/L2q+1(Z[pi],w1), the set of orbits of the action of L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) on the stable class.

accepted.question_text: Let q >= 3 and let xi: B -> BO be a fibration. For 2q-dimensional normal (q-1)-smoothings over (B,xi), let NS_xi(M,nu_bar) be the set of (B,xi)-diffeomorphism classes of normal smoothings bordant to (M,nu_bar) and having the same Euler characteristic. Each such smoothing has an extended quadratic Q_xi(q)-form mu(M,nu_bar) built from H_q(M; Z[pi]), the equivariant intersection form, and a quadratic refinement. Wall realisation gives an action of L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1), and the isometry class of the extended quadratic form is invariant under that action, giving a map mu from NS_xi(M,nu_bar)/L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1) to isometry classes of Q_xi(q)-forms. Is this map injective; equivalently, do any two bordant normal (q-1)-smoothings with equal Euler characteristic and isometric Q_xi(q)-forms differ by the action of L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1)?

evidence.quote: Hence the map above descends to define the map mu : NSxi(M,nu_bar)/L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) -> Hom(Z[pi],w1)(Qxi(q)).
Conjecture A. (The Q-form Conjecture for normal smoothings) If q >= 3, then the map mu of (2) is injective

accepted.question_text: Let q >= 3, let M be a closed connected compact 2q-manifold, let xi_M^{q-1}: B_M^{q-1} -> BO represent the normal (q-1)-type of M, and let S_st(M) be the stable class of M. The Q-form construction induces a map mu/aut(xi) from S_st(M)/L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1) to isometry classes of Q_{xi_M^{q-1}}(q)-forms modulo automorphisms of xi_M^{q-1}. Is this map injective; equivalently, for M0 and M1 in S_st(M), does M0 = rho M1 for some rho in L_{2q+1}(Z[pi],w1) hold exactly when M0 and M1 admit normal (q-1)-smoothings to B_M^{q-1} whose Q_{xi_M^{q-1}}(q)-forms are isometric?

evidence.quote: mu/aut(xi): Sst(M)/L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) -> Hom(Z[pi],w1)(Qxi_M^{q-1}(q))/aut(xi_M^{q-1}).
Conjecture B. (The Q-form Conjecture for the stable class) If q >= 3, then the map mu/aut(xi) of (3) is injective
